Subject: Tenant mapping, isolation confirmation & Private connectivity next steps

Hi Eliza —

Thanks again for your time on Friday. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture quick next steps so we can close the residency & connectivity questions for your security review. Attached are a tenant-mapping template and our PrivateLink readiness checklist to speed the handoff.

Ask list: 
- Could you populate the tenant mapping (logical tenant ID -> HealthLytics environment) and return the CSV? We use this to validate routing and RBAC boundaries.
- Confirm target hosting region(s) for production (you said EU for PHI; please specify region: eu-west-1 vs eu-central-1).
- Do you require a customer-managed key (BYOK/HSM) per tenant, or is a single HealthLytics key in your account acceptable?
- Any egress restrictions or specific destination IP ranges we should lock down for PrivateLink peering?

Proposed timeline: review returned mapping by 2027-06-14, PrivateLink smoke test week of 2027-06-21. If you need an earlier window we can shuffle resources.

Attachments: tenant-mapping-template.csv, privatelink-checklist.pdf

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0148

- Egress: we have a narrow set of outbound ranges; I included them in the mapping file (column: allowed_egress_cidr).

We can do the PrivateLink smoke test the week of 2027-06-21 — Thurs/Fri are best for our infra team.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Tenant mapping, isolation confirmation & Private connectivity next steps

Eliza / Stephanie —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts, Eliza. A few technical clarifications from Security so your team can complete the SIG/CIS/CAIQ pack quickly:

1) Key management
- If you remain with a HealthLytics-managed KMS key, please confirm whether you require separate key aliases per tenant (recommended for stricter separation) or a single key per environment.
- If you choose BYOK/HSM: which provider (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault HSM) and what rotation policy do you have? We need the key ARN/URI to include in the runbook.

2) Network and egress
- We will present a candidate set of IPs for the PrivateLink endpoint. Can you confirm whether you require outbound-only connections (no inbound) from our VPC to yours?
- For EU residency: our control plane will remain in our global control plane, but data plane for your workloads can be pinned to eu-central-1. We need to document: data-at-rest encryption, KV-cache persistence, and token retention windows.

3) Audit & logging
- Minimum requirement per your SOC2 scope: 1 year retention for access logs and 90 days for application traces by default. Do you need extended retention?

4) Dedicated/private options
- To remove ambiguity, we can offer either: a) Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool isolated to your org), or b) Redwood Private (VPC-local operator with customer-controlled peering). Please indicate preference; Dedicated gives faster onboarding but not customer-managed KMS in most cases.

Next steps: If you can confirm the points above we'll update the CAIQ and SIG answers and schedule the PrivateLink test. Happy to jump on a 30-min technical call with your infra lead; suggest Wed 2027-06-09 10:00 AM UTC if that works.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Security Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant mapping, isolation confirmation & Private connectivity next steps

Rishi / Stephanie —

Thanks — noted and answered inline: 
- Key management: we will start with a single HealthLytics-managed AWS KMS key per environment. If SOC2 requires tenant-level keys we will evaluate BYOK in Q3. Key ARN included in the mapping file (column: kms_key_arn).
- Egress: outbound-only (we do not want inbound connections into our VPC). The HL mapping CSV includes allowed outbound CIDRs.
- Retention: 1 year for access logs is fine. We will request extended trace retention only for forensics windows (rare).
- Dedicated vs Private: for this pilot we prefer Redwood Private (VPC-local operator) to keep the data plane fully within our peered environment. If you can share operator contact and runbook items we will coordinate.

I'll arrange a short call with our infra lead and send over a DocuSign link for the connectivity appendix tomorrow. Also, HealthLytics will fill out the SIG questionnaire — expect that in the next 48 hours.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/HL-PrivateLink-Contract-12345

Eliza
